$comment: The single place where this package knows pi's tool names.
Layer bodies reference capabilities as {{delegate}}, {{search}}, ... and never
name a tool directly — a test enforces that. When pi renames or drops a tool,
edit this file; the four layer bodies stay untouched.
required=true : a layer listing this capability in `requires-capabilities` is
skipped entirely when the tool is absent.
required=false: the tool is merely mentioned; when absent, `absent` is
substituted so no dead tool name survives into the prompt.
Deliberately excluded: read / grep / write / edit. They are pi's most primitive
tools (least likely to be renamed) and they are ordinary English words, so
placeholder-ing them would make the prose unreadable and the bare-name test useless.

code_search.absent: a `grep` sweep with several keyword guesses

code_nav.absent: `grep` for the symbol name and read the hits apart yourself

repo_map.absent: `ls` plus a few reads to work out what lives where

read_spans.absent: `read` on the files a search named

agents.name: explore
agents.use: read-only sweep at the cheap retrieval tier; returns compressed findings with file:line evidence. Send it when you cannot yet name the files a change touches, then write the brief from what it found. Cold only.

agents.name: plan
agents.use: read-only; turns a goal into a numbered list of steps. For when the decomposition itself depends on code nobody has read. Cold only.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.use: the worker that edits files. Give it a sidecar with a brief that names the code, or fork it when restating your context would cost more than a paragraph.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.use: read-only judgement machines cannot make: design quality, off-target work, security risk, arbitrating contradictory workers. Cold only — a reviewer holding your context confirms your reading instead of checking it.

agents.name: secretary
agents.use: closeout for any goal that changed the tree, and the only commit route: reconciles worktrees, branches and leftover artifacts, then commits the accepted paths. Its cleanup verdict is advisory; you still own the completion decision.
